items.title: Doc2Harness: Benchmarking LLMs on Long-Horizon Harness Engineering of Coding Agents
items.summary: Agents driven by large language models are increasingly deployed on long-horizon tasks, where they use tools and modify real workspaces. How well they perform depends as much on the harness around the model as on the model itself. items.summary: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. items.summary: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. items.summary: In long-horizon tool-calling tasks, LLM agents can fail not only because of tool-use errors, but also because of ineffective interaction with users.
